server_outdated.description: The server is {server} and BRAM here is {here}. Update the server: in Portainer, recreate the bram container with Re-pull image turned on.

integration_outdated.title: BRAM in Home Assistant is out of date
integration_outdated.description: BRAM here is {here} and the server is {server}. In HACS, update BRAM, then restart Home Assistant.

user.title: Pair with your BRAM Server
user.description: Open the BRAM Server's config page, press Get code, and paste the code here.

error.invalid_code: That code is wrong, expired, or already used.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that server, or it is not the one that made this code.

options.camera_away: A person while everyone is away
options.camera_door: A person at an open or unlocked door
options.camera_stranger: A person Frigate does not know

abort.no_people: Share a person with BRAM first.
abort.nothing_to_suggest: BRAM has no suggestions. It can see the important things.
abort.no_printers: BRAM did not find any 3D printers in Home Assistant.
abort.no_cameras: No cameras yet. Connect Frigate and turn on cameras under Settings, Cameras on BRAM's page, then come back.

init.title: BRAM
init.description: Choose what to set up. BRAM watches and tells you; it cannot control anything.

menu_option_descriptions.basic: Your phone and the main switches, on one page. Start here.
menu_option_descriptions.devices: What BRAM can see: suggestions, by type and room, or one by one.
menu_option_descriptions.alerts: Which phones get messages, quiet hours, and the daily summary.
menu_option_descriptions.watching: Home Assistant problems, locks, doors, and windows, 3D printers, and security.
menu_option_descriptions.chat: What the BRAM Server may read beyond live state: history, errors, security.
menu_option_descriptions.learn: Let BRAM suggest better night hours from how your home is used.

basic.title: Quick setup

data.night: Tell me if a lock is unlocked at night (10 PM to 6 AM)
data.left_open: Tell me if a door is left open (10 minutes)
data.offline: Tell me if a lock or door sensor goes offline
data.problem_watch: Tell me about problems with Home Assistant
data.share_history: Let BRAM look into the history of what it can see

data_description.skip: Anything you pick here is not shared. Leave it empty to share everything listed above.

quick.title: Add by type and room
quick.description: BRAM looks for devices it understands. You choose which to share on the next page.

data.areas: Only in these areas (empty means everywhere)

review.title: Choose what to share
review.description:
Found {count}. All of these will be shared:
{found}

data_description.skip: Anything you pick here is not shared. Leave it empty to share everything listed above.

see.title: Choose one by one
see.description: Only what you choose here is shared with BRAM. It cannot control any of it.

rooms.title: People's rooms
rooms.description: You usually do not need this: BRAM finds these by itself. Change one only if a person shows the wrong room. Each is the sensor that says which room they are in.

chat.title: Server access
chat.description: Lets the BRAM Server read more than live state, to answer your questions and fill its history. Nothing here changes what BRAM watches. Problems sends short summaries with passwords, tokens, and addresses removed; removal cannot catch everything. The security check sends findings and device names, never account names.

data_description.share_history: On: answers such as when a door last opened, and past temperatures brought into BRAM's history. 10 days of shared devices only.
data_description.share_problems: On: answers such as which integrations are failing.
data_description.share_security: On: you can ask whether your home is secure.

learn.title: Learning
learn.description:
BRAM reads from its history when your home goes quiet at night and how long doors stay open, then suggests better night hours and left-open times. It needs Keep history on, on BRAM's page. Your phone gets a message that opens the review page. Nothing changes until you approve one.

Nights found so far: {nights} of the 14 needed. A night counts at noon after it.

data.undo: Undo the last change I approved

data_description.learn: Checked: BRAM suggests better hours from its history. Unchecked: no suggestions.
data_description.undo: Puts back the hours you had before you approved the last suggestion.
data_description.forget: Your current hours stay as they are. Only nights from today on count, and BRAM forgets any waiting suggestion and your Never answers. History itself is kept.

watch.title: Locks, doors, windows, and motion
watch.description: For the locks, doors, windows, garage doors, and motion sensors BRAM can see. Each is off until you turn it on.

data.offline: A lock or door sensor goes offline

data_description.night: Uses your night hours below. Ignores quiet hours.

doors.name: Doors and windows
doors.description: Choose which kinds count, then what to be told about them.

data.open_minutes: Left open means this many minutes

data_description.left_open: Told when one stays open longer than the minutes below.
data_description.open_windows: Turn off if you sleep with windows open.
data_description.open_night: Told when one is open in your night hours. Ignores quiet hours.
data_description.open_climate: Told when one stays open longer than the minutes above while a thermostat is heating or cooling.

away.name: While everyone is away
away.description: Away counts only the people BRAM can see, so share everyone who lives here. These ignore quiet hours.

data.away: A lock unlocked, or a door or window open

data_description.away: Every door and window counts here, whatever you chose above.
data_description.motion_away: Told once per sensor until someone is home again. Pets can set this off.

data.weekend_night_from: Friday and Saturday night starts (empty: same)
data.weekend_night_to: Friday and Saturday night ends (empty: same)
data.asleep: Also night while any of these is on

data_description.asleep: Optional. A helper or sensor that is on while someone is asleep, such as a bedtime switch. Night then starts when it turns on, even before your hours. If it is unavailable, only the hours count.

alerts.title: Messages
alerts.description: Safety alerts come from Home Assistant itself and ignore quiet hours. They do not replace certified alarms.

data.safety_phones: Phones that get safety alerts only
data.escalate: Also use Telegram and ntfy if nobody answers a safety alert in 5 minutes

printers.title: 3D printers
printers.description: BRAM found these printers in Home Assistant. It only watches; it cannot start, stop, or heat anything.

data_description.printers: On: progress on Home, and you are told when a print finishes, fails, or pauses, or a heater is left on. Only the printers you switch on below are watched or shown.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Only what you share is seen by BRAM, and it cannot control any of it.

menu_option_descriptions.suggest: The important things BRAM cannot see yet, such as locks, doors, and safety sensors.
menu_option_descriptions.quick: Find everything of a type, such as lights or motion, in the rooms you pick.
menu_option_descriptions.see: Everything BRAM can see, by group. Add or remove one at a time.
menu_option_descriptions.rooms: Only if a person shows the wrong room. BRAM normally finds this itself.

watching.title: Watching
watching.description: Each is off until you turn it on. Safety alerts for leak, smoke, and gas sensors you share are always on.

menu_option_descriptions.watch_ha: Failed integrations, errors, batteries, offline devices, backups, and new admins or tokens.
menu_option_descriptions.watch: Unlocked at night, open while away, left open, open at night, open while heating or cooling, motion while away, and offline, with your night hours.
menu_option_descriptions.printers: Prints finishing, failing, or pausing, and heaters left on, for each printer you choose.
menu_option_descriptions.comfort: Too hot, too cold, near freezing, and humid, for the rooms BRAM can see.
menu_option_descriptions.cameras: A person while everyone is away or at night, someone Frigate does not know, and packages.

watch_ha.title: Home Assistant and security
watch_ha.description: What BRAM finds is sent to the BRAM Server for Findings, with passwords, tokens, and addresses removed. Removal cannot catch everything.

data.security_watch: Run the security check every 10 minutes

data_description.problem_watch: On: you are told about failed integrations, repeating errors, low batteries, offline devices, broken automations, old backups, and a full disk.
data_description.security_watch: On: you are told once about anything new, such as an administrator or access token, a failed sign-in, or a lock exposed to a voice assistant.

comfort.title: Temperature and humidity
comfort.description: Covers the temperature and humidity sensors and thermostats BRAM can see. A room must stay past its limit for 30 minutes, or 15 minutes near freezing. Near freezing ignores quiet hours. Leave out sensors that are outside.

data_description.comfort_skip: Outdoor sensors, freezers, attics, and others that are meant to be hot or cold.

camera_rules.title: Cameras
camera_rules.description: For the cameras you turn on under Settings, Cameras on BRAM's page, which reads Frigate. The Frigate integration {frigate} installed here; with it, each message shows Frigate's picture.

data.camera_away: A person while everyone is away
data.camera_stranger: A person Frigate does not know
data.camera_repeat: Not again on the same camera for
data.camera_door: A person at a door that is open or unlocked

data_description.camera_away: Away counts only the people BRAM can see. Ignores quiet hours.
data_description.camera_night: Uses your night hours under Locks, doors, and windows. Ignores quiet hours.
data_description.camera_stranger: Only useful with face recognition on in Frigate; without it, every person is unknown.
data_description.camera_repeat: One person walking past several cameras is also one message.
data_description.camera_door: Link each camera to its doors under Set up one camera. Ignores quiet hours.
data_description.camera_car: Only a car that stays at least 30 seconds, so one driving past is left out. Choose its zones, such as the driveway, under Set up one camera.

cameras.title: Cameras
cameras.description: BRAM's server reads Frigate for the cameras you turn on under Settings, Cameras on BRAM's page. Choose what to be told about, then set up each camera.

menu_option_descriptions.camera_rules: A person while everyone is away, at an open or unlocked door, or at night; a stranger; a package; a car.
menu_option_descriptions.camera_pick: The doors a camera looks at, the Frigate zones that count, and which messages it sends.
menu_option_descriptions.watching: To the other things BRAM watches.

camera_one.title: Camera: {camera}
camera_one.description: Each message also has to be turned on under What to tell me.

data.doors: Doors and locks this camera looks at

data_description.doors: For a person at a door that is open or unlocked.
data_description.zones: Frigate's zones for this camera, such as porch or driveway. Empty: the whole picture counts. With zones, a person or car outside them is left out.
data_description.rules: Leave all chosen to use every message you turned on.
